clue.text: Boasted about grub missing last crop

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the shortened word for grub round
missing last says the final letter of the grub word is dropped

parts.note: tuck is British slang for food, especially schoolboy snacks

explanation.surface: Someone who bragged has given up food, all except a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boasted' uses the old past tense: 'the cock crew'. 'Missing last' trims the grub word, and 'about' turns the remainder round; 'crop' is a haircut, not a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, and a crop is likewise a close-cut hairstyle.

clue.text: New scout master's convention

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of scout are made into something fresh

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for master, as in MA degrees

explanation.surface: A fresh scout leader has a traditional way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal working on 'scout' alone; 'master's' supplies its abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is an established practice, a social convention that people follow.

clue.text: Titular person's upset by setter's emphatic refusal

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the joined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so setter's gives my
nope is an emphatic, informal no

explanation.surface: A title character is annoyed by the compiler saying a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: MY + NOPE turned round by 'upset' gives EPONYM; the 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is a person after whom something is named, so they are the titular figure.

clue.text: More than able to finish off with sex

definitions.meaning: as an adjective the word means supremely skilled, far beyond merely competent
as a verb it means to complete a marriage by first sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: Being highly capable of completing things in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means accomplished in the highest degree; the verb means to complete a marriage physically.

clue.text: Yes, it's up — no, it's down!

definitions.text: Yes, it's up — no, it's down!

parts.words: Yes, it's up — no, it's down!
parts.note: describes the digit raised to signal approval and lowered to signal rejection

explanation.surface: Someone flip-flopping on whether something is rising or falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit held upward means approval and pointed downward means rejection, as in the Roman arena.

clue.text: Rural spelling bee, you see? Oh 'ell, I see!

parts.note: bee is the name of the letter B
you sounds like the letter U
see sounds like the letter C
oh sounds like the letter O
ell is the name of the letter L
see again sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: A country spelling bee contestant reciting letters and exclaiming in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' tells you the clue spells out letter names: bee, you, see, oh, 'ell, I, see give the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic describes pastoral countryside life, so it is a synonym for rural.

clue.text: What the Parisian does to 11 to be square

parts.note: the French article le splits the word even, giving the number eleven, which is what clue 11 points to

explanation.surface: A Frenchman doing something to a number so that accounts balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisian' is LE; put inside EVEN it makes E-LE-VEN, so LE breaks EVEN to give 11.
explanation.definitionFit: To break even is to finish with neither profit nor loss, leaving one square.

clue.text: Grind nut as wanted

indicators.note: wanted here means lacking, so the letters of as are missing

parts.note: a cashew is a kind of nut

explanation.surface: Someone milling nuts exactly as required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted' looks like 'desired' but means 'lacking': CASHEW lacking AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew is to grind food between the teeth.

clue.text: Dating doesn't start 'til after work for one in suit

indicators.note: work signals that the letters are worked into a new order
doesn't start says the first letter of dating is dropped

parts.note: til is a shortened form of until

explanation.surface: Romance is postponed until the end of the working day for someone in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: ATING (dating less D) and TIL are rearranged together by 'work'; 'after' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigant is a party to a lawsuit, so is someone involved in a suit.

clue.text: One helping to control fish where they're mostly coarse

parts.note: cod is a common sea fish
coarse fish, the freshwater kinds anglers catch, are mostly found in rivers

explanation.surface: A fishing guide talks about where coarse fish live.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'coarse fish' are freshwater fish other than salmon and trout, so their home is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-driver shares driving duties, helping to steer and control a vehicle, especially in rallying.

clue.text: Fleeced Irishman in Blarney?

indicators.note: Blarney is Irish talk, so the Irish name is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: Was an Irish smooth talker the one who robbed someone?
explanation.walkthrough: Blarney is persuasive Irish chatter; said aloud, SEAN sounds like SHORN in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleeced sheep has had its wool cut off, and shorn means exactly that.

clue.text: Quango is so badly cut with needle

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A government body is described as slashed with a sharp instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A quango is a British quasi-autonomous public body, run by appointees rather than voted-in members.
explanation.definitionFit: Quango board members are appointed rather than voted in, so such a body is not chosen by election.

clue.text: Only line omitted by Guardian's second old president? Get outta here!

indicators.note: omitted says the letter for line is left out of only

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself says our
B denotes second class or grade
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A president of yesteryear is told brusquely to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply joins the pieces; ONLY without L gives ONY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British idiom telling someone to go away, much like get outta here.

clue.text: Produce held back by nail guns

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables are delayed by construction tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' signals the letters lie in 'nail guns': ILGU read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a citrus fruit, and produce means fruit and vegetables collectively.

clue.text: Indecent to flash by running stream without pausing

parts.note: blue means risqué or smutty
to streak is to run naked in public

explanation.surface: A naked runner dashes rudely past a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is a link; talking a blue streak means talking rapidly and incessantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue streak is an unbroken rapid flow, as of talk, something running on nonstop.

clue.text: Evil one quits wife-beating?

indicators.note: quits says the letter for one leaves the phrase

parts.note: the question mark flags male violence as an example of wife-beating
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wicked man gives up domestic abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE VIOLENCE with the I removed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is ill will or wickedness, a noun for evil.

clue.text: Crustacean could be gelatinous without one

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of gelatinous may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shellfish might turn jelly-like without a certain ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: GELATINOUS minus I ('without one') gives letters that rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, a type of crustacean.

clue.text: Put up a fight when dumped

definitions.meaning: to scrap is to fight or brawl, so this is its past tense

explanation.surface: Someone fought back when they were jilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapped is the past of scrap, both to brawl and to discard as useless.

clue.text: Whisper about USSR capturing American city once

indicators.note: capturing means the jumbled letters enclose the old city
about tells us the letters of USSR are moved around

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Murmurs about the Soviet Union seizing an American city in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: USSR rearranged as SUSR takes in UR, giving SUSURR, then US is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A susurrus is a soft whispering or rustling sound.

clue.text: Bear's face

definitions.meaning: to bear is to tolerate or allow
a face is a person's features or expression

explanation.surface: Describing the features of a large furry animal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to tolerate; as a noun it means a person's face.

clue.text: Now and then spot this in the playground

parts.note: spot in the present tense, now, is see
spot in the past tense, then, is saw

explanation.surface: Occasionally you notice something at the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' looks like 'occasionally' but asks for present and past forms of a verb meaning spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a balancing plank that children ride in playgrounds.

clue.text: Anger consumes team lifted by tonic

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the letters are read upwards
consumes means the anger word swallows the team

parts.note: to rile is to anger
XI is eleven, the size of a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: A team gets annoyed and drinks a restorative.
explanation.walkthrough: RILE takes in XI to give RIXILE, and 'lifted' turns it up to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure-all, a medicinal tonic.

clue.text: Compound soulless LP

indicators.note: soulless means losing the heart, the central letter

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record, an album

explanation.surface: A record with no soul is a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'soul' of ALBUM is its middle letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate used in dyeing and tanning.

clue.text: Bill enacted by this statesman

parts.note: Old Bill is British slang for the police, and the Home Secretary who founded the Met is meant

explanation.surface: A piece of legislation was passed by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Bill' is not legislation but the Old Bill, the police force created by this Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: The statesman founded London's Metropolitan Police in 1829, whose officers became known as bobbies and peelers.

clue.text: Where to keep so many pens?

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to store a large number of writing implements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing tools but is the verb 'encloses'. Epsom is a Surrey racecourse town, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a place, so it can stand for where in a clue about location.

clue.text: Slight indistinction of speech

definitions.meaning: a slight is an insult or insinuation
slurring is running words together indistinctly

explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both an insulting remark and a blurred way of pronouncing words.

clue.text: Inability to move capital stopped by a sly transfer

indicators.note: stopped by means the capital is plugged by the rearranged letters

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: transfer suggests the letters of a sly are moved around

explanation.surface: A city is brought to a standstill by a cunning move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfer' rearranges 'a sly' into ALYS, and 'stopped by' means the capital is plugged with those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralysis is loss of the power to move.

clue.text: Two letters delivered in county

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, so we hear the letters said aloud

parts.note: the two letters are S and X, which together sound like the county

explanation.surface: A pair of letters arrive in a rural district.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; said aloud, S and X give its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the English counties.

clue.text: Duet sees review that evens out merit

indicators.note: evens out means the even-numbered letters are removed, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: A pair of performers read a critique that balances things.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of 'Duet sees review'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve is to merit, to be worthy of something.

clue.text: A garden location comes in to spoil the antithesis of hippy philosophy

indicators.note: comes in means these letters go inside the word for spoil

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
Kew is home to the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: A garden spot interferes with the anti-hippy credo.
explanation.walkthrough: A + KEW goes into MAR; Kew Gardens are London's famous botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippies said make love, not war; to fight is the opposite of that slogan.
